subject: IME status: repro done, interpretability tax quantified
body:
Dmitri, Jelena,

Status. Repro complete on both datasets with num_experts=20: IME_BW (LSTM assignment) matches the released numbers on Rossmann and ECL; IME_WW (linear assignment) lands where expected, slightly behind BW. Amara's synthetic pipeline is generating regime-switching series that match the internal workload's autocorrelation and seasonality profile well - the data owner's team eyeballed the marginals and signed off on fidelity.

The finding that will shape the recommendation: single-expert assignment at inference costs about 4% RMSE versus soft mixing on the synthetic bed when regimes overlap heavily, but under 1% when regimes are cleanly separated. Our internal workload looks like the clean case, fortunately. Also, smoothness_hp at 0.01 matters more than we expected - dropping it produces expert-flapping, where consecutive timesteps flip experts and the 'explanation' becomes noise. Efe wants flap-rate reported as a first-class metric alongside RMSE, which I support.

On track for mid-July internal eval.

Kaia
